articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. trade sparks Asante Samuel Sr. warning as Cowboys star faces pressure after leaving Steelers
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr. is getting a fresh start with the Dallas Cowboys, but former NFL cornerback Asante Samuel Sr.
articles.body: Joey Porter Jr. is getting a fresh start with the Dallas Cowboys, but former NFL cornerback Asante Samuel Sr. believes the young defensive back may have been better off staying with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Dallas acquired Porter from Pittsburgh in a trade this week after a long contract dispute kept him off the field for the first three games of the 2026 season. The Cowboys sent the Steelers a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick for the 26-year-old cornerback. Soon after the deal became official, Samuel shared his view on X, warning Porter that leaving Pittsburgh does not automatically mean things will work out better in Dallas. Porter now has a chance to put the entire contract situation behind him and focus on his new team, with the Cowboys preparing to face the Houston Texans in Week 4.Why did Asante Samuel Sr. question Joey Porter Jr.’s move to the Dallas Cowboys?Samuel did not hide his thoughts after the trade. The former New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles cornerback wrote on X, “IDK… Joey Porter Jr. should’ve thugged it out in Pittsburgh. The grass isn’t always greener on the other side. Let’s see how this plays out.” His message came shortly after the Steelers and Cowboys completed the deal.The comment is interesting because Porter had spent the offseason trying to reach a new contract with Pittsburgh. The Steelers selected him in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, and he quickly became an important part of their defense. According to the NFL, Porter played 47 games and made 41 starts during his three seasons in Pittsburgh. He finished that stretch with 165 tackles, three interceptions and 31 passes defended.Porter was entering the final year of his rookie contract when the dispute with Pittsburgh continued into the regular season. He also dealt with a back issue during training camp and missed the Steelers’ first three games. The NFL reported that his status had also been connected to conditioning as the situation developed.Now, instead of trying to settle the issue in Pittsburgh, Porter will have to prove himself with Dallas. The Cowboys made the move because they needed help in the secondary, with injuries affecting the cornerback group. The Dallas Cowboys said Porter gives the team a young outside corner who already has 41 NFL starts.What does Joey Porter Jr.’s move mean for the Dallas Cowboys?Porter arrives in Dallas with plenty to prove, but he also brings three seasons of starting experience. In 2025, he started all 14 games he played and recorded 52 tackles, one interception and a team-high 14 passes defended for Pittsburgh, according to the Pittsburgh Steelers.The Cowboys are 1-2 heading into their Week 4 meeting with the Houston Texans, and their secondary has already dealt with injuries. Dallas has also gone without an interception through its first three games.Porter could make his Cowboys debut against Houston on Sunday, October 4, although his playing status will depend on how quickly he settles in with the team and how coaches assess his condition. He has said his back feels better after missing the opening games of the season.For Porter, the trade creates a completely different situation. He is no longer dealing directly with the Steelers’ contract talks, but he also does not have a new long-term deal with Dallas. That means his performance could become an important part of what happens next in his career.Samuel’s warning, then, is not necessarily about whether Porter can succeed in Dallas. It is a reminder that changing teams does not guarantee an easier path. Porter now has an opportunity to show that the move was the right step for him, beginning with his new life in Dallas.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why does Josh Allen have Hailee Steinfeld feeling ‘a little ’stitious’; Patriots reveal their biggest problem with Bills QB
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld did not reveal a secret game-day ritual for Josh Allen.
articles.body: Hailee Steinfeld did not reveal a secret game-day ritual for Josh Allen. She did admit there is some superstition involved when her husband takes the field.The timing makes the confession more interesting. Allen and the Buffalo Bills are 3-0 entering their Oct. 4 matchup with the New England Patriots, whose defensive coordinator just described one part of defending the quarterback as “the hardest thing in football to defend.”Why is Hailee Steinfeld ‘a little ’stitious’ when Josh Allen plays?During a Sept. 30 appearance on “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon,” Steinfeld was asked whether she and Allen get superstitious around his games.Her answer was short.“We're a little 'stitious, you know? How can you not be?” Steinfeld said.She did not elaborate on any specific ritual, so there is no lucky outfit, meal or pregame routine to dissect just yet.Whatever superstition exists is arriving during an unbeaten start for Buffalo. The Bills have opened the season 3-0, with Allen continuing to affect games through both the air and on the ground.The couple has also had plenty happening away from football.Steinfeld and Allen married in Montecito, Calif., in May 2025. They welcomed their daughter, Harper Haize Allen, in April 2026.Steinfeld later wrote about Harper in the Mother's Day edition of her Beau Society newsletter.“Dearest Harper, I’m in awe of you,” Steinfeld wrote. “You’ve been here for only a short while now, and somehow it feels as though you’ve always been ours.”Her Sept. 30 appearance also came during a press run for the Disney film “Hexed,” which is scheduled for release Nov. 26.Allen's next assignment comes much sooner.Buffalo hosts New England at 1 p.m. ET on Oct. 4 at Highmark Stadium, and the Patriots have already made clear that containing the Bills quarterback requires more than defending the original play.What makes Josh Allen’s ‘second play’ so difficult for the Patriots to defend?New England defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr gave Allen one of the strongest compliments an opposing coach can give a quarterback this week.According to Boston Herald reporter Andrew Callahan, Kuhr called Allen an “MVP-caliber quarterback playing MVP football.”But Kuhr's larger concern comes after Buffalo's designed play begins to fall apart.Pats Pulpit's Brian Hines reported that Kuhr described defending Allen's improvisational “second play” as “the hardest thing in football to defend.”That is where Allen creates a different problem.A defense can disrupt the original call and still lose the rep if Allen escapes pressure. Coverage has to hold longer, rushers have to maintain their lanes and defenders must account for Allen as a runner.His numbers through three games show why.Allen has thrown for 786 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions. He has added 114 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the ground, according to StatMuse.That rushing threat forces New England to defend more than Buffalo's passing concepts.The Patriots have seen the problem before. Last season, with Kuhr serving as New England's defensive play-caller, the Patriots held Buffalo to 20 points in a road victory. Patriots.com later detailed how New England mixed man coverage, zone pressures and a dedicated spy on Allen.Buffalo and New England ultimately split their two meetings last season.Now the Patriots return to Buffalo at 1-2 and coming off a 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Bills remain unbeaten.That puts Steinfeld's “little 'stitious” admission on one side of Sunday’s matchup.On the other is a Patriots coaching staff trying to solve something far more concrete: what happens when the first plan for stopping Josh Allen stops working.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Could ESPN replace Troy Aikman with Pat McAfee and Peyton Manning on ‘Monday Night Football’
articles.summary: Troy Aikman expected his ESPN future to be settled before the 2026 NFL season. It was not.
articles.body: Troy Aikman expected his ESPN future to be settled before the 2026 NFL season. It was not.Now, with the Hall of Fame quarterback entering the final year of his contract, Jason Whitlock has floated a dramatic alternative for “Monday Night Football”: Pat McAfee and Peyton Manning joining Joe Buck in place of Aikman.Why is Troy Aikman’s ESPN future still unresolved?Aikman joined ESPN alongside Buck in 2022 after signing a reported five-year, $90 million contract. The pair had already spent two decades together at Fox before making the move to “Monday Night Football.”Buck has since secured his own new deal. EssentiallySports reported that the play-by-play broadcaster agreed to a six-year, $108 million extension.Aikman has not received the same resolution.Speaking with Richard Deitsch last month, Aikman said he expected his contract situation to be handled before the season began.“I thought something would be done prior to the start of this season. I’ve never gone into a last year of a contract ever, since I signed with the Dallas Cowboys, so I thought that it would be done. It’s not.”He added that he had not spoken with ESPN executives about what Buck’s extension meant for him.“I’ve had no conversation with anyone from Bristol as far as what this means for me.”Buck has made his preference clear.During an appearance on Philadelphia’s 97.5 The Fanatic, he said he remains hopeful that ESPN and Aikman will reach an agreement.“I legitimately love the guy like a brother. We’re basically the same age; I’m 57, he’s 59. We’ve both been through divorce. We’re both girl dads. 25 years, you’re sharing a lot of life together. Forget games and in the booth and all that stuff.”Buck later added: “I’m obviously hopeful, to say the least, that something gets done.”ESPN has not announced a replacement plan.Josh Krulewitz, ESPN’s executive vice president of communications, told EssentiallySports that the network would not discuss talent contracts before its upcoming Super Bowl broadcast.“With this historic season for ESPN now underway, our entire focus is on bringing fans the best possible football coverage, culminating with our first Super Bowl,” Krulewitz said. “To that end, we won’t be addressing talent contract specifics before the Super Bowl.”Could Pat McAfee and Peyton Manning actually replace Troy Aikman on ‘Monday Night Football’?The McAfee-Manning scenario currently comes from Whitlock, not ESPN.On his “Fearless With Jason Whitlock” podcast, Whitlock pointed to Aikman’s stalled negotiations and McAfee’s growing presence across ESPN programming.“Troy Aikman hasn’t got a new contract. His talks are on hold,” Whitlock said. “Pat McAfee, they’ve been sprinkling everywhere on ESPN. Why not Monday Night Football? He was a player in the National Football League. But let me put this twist on it. I wouldn’t put Pat McAfee opposite Joe Buck. But I would put Pat McAfee and Peyton Manning opposite Joe Buck.”Whitlock later called the idea a “real possibility” and argued that the pairing could work because McAfee and Manning already know each other from their time with the Indianapolis Colts.McAfee’s role at ESPN has continued to expand. He joined the “Monday Night Countdown” crew this season while remaining one of the network’s most visible personalities.Manning already has an established relationship with ESPN through the “ManningCast,” which he hosts with his brother Eli Manning during select “Monday Night Football” games.Still, there is an important distinction. No report cited here says ESPN is negotiating with McAfee and Manning to replace Aikman.Whitlock is proposing the pairing while Aikman’s contract remains unsettled.That uncertainty matters because Buck and Aikman have called games together since 2002. Their partnership includes more than 290 regular-season games, over 40 playoff games and six Super Bowls.Aikman has also said he wants that partnership to continue.Asked whether Buck’s extension would affect his own decision, Aikman said: “Would I want to continue to work with Joe Buck moving down the road? 100 percent.”For now, ESPN has Aikman in the booth and no announced successor. The intrigue comes from what happens after the season, especially if the network and its longtime analyst still cannot agree on a new contract.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Can Jared Goff pass Joe Montana on Sunday night? Lions QB needs just 128 yards against Panthers
articles.summary: Jared Goff needs only 128 passing yards Sunday night to move past Joe Montana on the NFL’s all-time regular-season list.
articles.body: Jared Goff needs only 128 passing yards Sunday night to move past Joe Montana on the NFL’s all-time regular-season list. His chance comes against a Carolina Panthers defense missing both starting cornerbacks.The Detroit Lions quarterback enters Week 4 with 40,424 career passing yards, according to Lions On SI’s John Maakaron. Montana finished his career with 40,551, leaving one of football’s biggest names directly ahead of Goff at No. 24.How close is Jared Goff to passing Joe Montana on the NFL career passing list?The math is simple. Goff sits 127 yards behind Montana, meaning 128 yards against Carolina would move him into 24th place.For Goff, the name attached to the milestone matters.The former No. 1 overall pick grew up in California as a San Francisco 49ers fan. Montana led the 49ers to four Super Bowl championships and became one of the defining quarterbacks of his era.When reporters asked Goff this week about potentially passing Montana, he immediately acknowledged that connection.“Yeah, that's awesome. I think you play long enough, you start getting into those volume numbers like that and very cool. Yeah, absolutely something cool moment. And like you said, grew up in the Bay and Joe's obviously the man there and that's awesome.”Goff has reached this point through 11 NFL seasons with the Los Angeles Rams and Lions. He also enters Sunday's game after another productive outing.The quarterback completed 25 of 32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns in Detroit's 31-24 win over the New York Jets in Week 3. Through three games, Goff has yet to throw an interception.Durability has helped him steadily climb the career list. Goff has missed only three games since joining Detroit, with all three absences coming in 2021.He told reporters that remaining available is something he takes seriously.“Yeah. I do take a lot of pride in that, being on the field," said Goff. "And I take a lot less of a beating than all these other guys out there. And for them to fight and be on the field, I owe them the same thing for me to make sure my body's ready. I do a lot of work in the offseason and take care of myself the right way, eat the right things."You can only do so much. There are things that happen, but I do try to put my best foot forward every day and every offseason.”Now, the next name within reach happens to be Montana.Why could the Panthers’ injured secondary give Jared Goff his opening Sunday night?Goff will get his shot against a Carolina secondary suddenly short on established options.The Associated Press reported that the Panthers placed starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson on injured reserve Wednesday. Horn is dealing with a quadriceps injury, while Jackson has a groin injury. Both are expected to miss about eight weeks.Carolina is expected to turn to Akayleb Evans and rookie Will Lee III. Evans has made 15 career starts, although only two have come since 2024. Lee is preparing for his first NFL start.Athlon Sports reported that the injuries left Carolina with only three healthy cornerbacks on its 53-man roster.That matters against a Lions offense that has scored exactly 31 points in all three games this season.Still, Carolina has already shown it can overcome major personnel losses. Last November, the Panthers faced Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams without three defensive starters, including Horn. Carolina forced Stafford into three turnovers and won 31-28.Panthers coach Dave Canales is again putting the responsibility on the replacements.“People say next man up, and that’s really what it is,” Canales said. “I go to the excitement for the opportunity for the guys that are going to play. These opportunities are few and far between, and so ... when guys have a chance to come in and contribute to the team, it changes them. It energizes them."Detroit enters Sunday at 2-1, while Carolina is 1-2. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.Goff does not need a career night to rewrite one line of the NFL record book. One hundred twenty-eight yards puts him ahead of Joe Montana.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Urban Meyer gives Ryan Day blunt Ohio State warning before Iowa clash after Buckeyes defense allows 462 yards
articles.summary: Former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer has pointed to one area that could make Saturday’s game against Iowa much harder for Ryan Day and the Buckeyes.
articles.body: Former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer has pointed to one area that could make Saturday’s game against Iowa much harder for Ryan Day and the Buckeyes. Meyer believes Iowa must find a way to move the ball against Ohio State’s defense if it wants to make the game close. The warning comes after Iowa’s 20-19 win over Michigan and Ohio State’s 42-19 victory over Illinois.What is Urban Meyer warning Ryan Day about before Ohio State faces Iowa?Meyer made his point on his Triple Option podcast while looking ahead to Ohio State’s trip to Kinnick Stadium. He does not think Iowa can rely on another low scoring game if it wants to stay with the Buckeyes.“If it’s all on Iowa’s offense, you can’t do against Ohio State what they’ve done other times,” Meyer said. “This can’t be a 10 point, one touchdown game. Even against the Wolverines, one of the touchdowns was a kickoff return. Ohio State’s too good to do that. But if Iowa can move the ball, this would be a street fight.”The former Buckeyes coach sees a clear battle between Iowa’s defense and Ohio State’s offense. But he also believes Iowa’s ability to run the ball could decide whether the game stays close.“It’s going to be strength on strength: Ohio State’s offense against Iowa’s defense,” Meyer said. “How can Iowa move the ball where Ohio State’s defense has at times shown some vulnerability? If they can do this, it will be a very close game. If they can’t, I think it’s a two score win for the Buckeyes.”That defensive concern is worth watching because Ohio State allowed Illinois to gain 462 total yards in the Buckeyes’ 42-19 win. Illinois also ran for 199 yards. Ohio State won comfortably because its offense was excellent, but the defensive numbers gave Meyer a reason to focus on that side of the ball.Can Ryan Day’s Ohio State defense handle Iowa’s rushing attack?Iowa enters the matchup at 4-0 after its late 20-19 win over Michigan. Ohio State is 3-1 after losing to Texas before responding with wins over Kent State and Illinois. The Buckeyes are ranked No. 5, while Iowa is No. 14 heading into the meeting.Ohio State has plenty of firepower on offense. Quarterback Julian Sayin threw for 367 yards and four touchdowns against Illinois, while wide receiver Jeremiah Smith caught 12 passes for 217 yards and four touchdowns. Smith’s four touchdown catches tied an Ohio State single game record.Iowa, however, brings a different challenge. The Hawkeyes have been one of the better rushing teams in the country, and their defense has also kept opponents from scoring freely. That makes this a difficult matchup for both sides rather than a simple test of Ohio State’s offense.Meyer also understands the pressure around Day better than most. Day worked under Meyer at Ohio State before taking over as head coach. Since then, Day has dealt with high expectations in Columbus, even after leading the Buckeyes to a national championship last season.Now, Ohio State heads into Iowa City with another demanding road game. Meyer’s message is simple: if the Buckeyes allow Iowa to run its offense comfortably, the game could become much tighter than expected. articles.title: Pablo Torre questions Tim Tebow over Life Surge allegations as investigation puts Christian organization under scrutiny
articles.summary: Pablo Torre has criticized Tim Tebow and other sports figures connected to Life Surge after his investigation raised questions about the Christian
articles.body: Pablo Torre has criticized Tim Tebow and other sports figures connected to Life Surge after his investigation raised questions about the Christian financial organization’s sales practices. Torre said he contacted the sports personalities for comment and questioned whether they were concerned about how their names and images were used. Tebow has since paused his relationship with Life Surge and said his team is investigating the allegations.Pablo Torre questions Tim Tebow over Life Surge responseTorre made the comments after working with Mother Jones reporter Kiera Butler on an investigation into Life Surge, a faith-based company that runs large events focused on Christianity, motivation and money. Their reporting examined complaints from people who said they were pushed toward expensive financial training after attending the events.Torre said he wanted answers from Tebow and other sports figures whose names were connected to Life Surge. “All the sports figures got requests for comment from us at this point,” Torre said on his YouTube channel. He then questioned whether the people involved felt troubled by the use of their names and images.“What we want to know is does this bother you? Does any of this bother you?” Torre said. He added that the reaction should be more than simply calling the situation embarrassing, saying, “It’s, I presume also something like your conscience reminding you that this is f***ed up.”The investigation reported that Tebow had appeared at dozens of Life Surge events since 2021. Mother Jones and Pablo Torre Finds Out also reported that some attendees were later offered more costly programs, with advanced training reported to reach tens of thousands of dollars. The investigation also said former attendees described feeling pressured to spend far more than they had planned after being introduced to higher-priced programs during those same Life Surge events.Tim Tebow pauses Life Surge relationship amid allegationsTebow has not admitted taking part in any wrongdoing. After the allegations became public, he said he was taking the matter seriously and would step away while his team looked into the claims.“The allegations are extremely, extremely serious, and it’s something that we take very serious,” Tebow said. “So, for us, we’re having our team do an investigation, but also pausing our relationship ‘til we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more.”The Washington Post, citing an Associated Press report, confirmed Tebow’s decision to pause the relationship. The report said Tebow spoke before a Florida game on September 25.Life Surge has also disputed the way its business practices have been described. The company said it does not train sales staff to pressure customers into borrowing money they cannot afford and said its headline speakers are not asked to promote its advanced training programs.Pablo Torre and Kiera Butler also reported that they reviewed complaints filed with the Federal Trade Commission. Those complaints are allegations from consumers and are not, by themselves, findings that Life Surge broke the law.The issue now centers on what the investigation found, what Life Surge says in response, and how the public figures associated with the organization explain their involvement.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lane Kiffin reveals how Trey’Dez Green became Sam Leavitt’s comfort zone before LSU faced another injury setback
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin has admitted that losing Trey’Dez Green took away Sam Leavitt’s most trusted option at LSU.
articles.body: Lane Kiffin has admitted that losing Trey’Dez Green took away Sam Leavitt’s most trusted option at LSU. Green has missed time with an injury, leaving Leavitt to build new connections in the passing game. The quarterback then played through a hamstring injury in LSU’s 35-6 win over Texas A&M, but still threw for 312 yards and two touchdowns. Kiffin said Green had been Leavitt’s “comfort zone.”Lane Kiffin explains Sam Leavitt’s lost comfort zoneGreen was hurt during LSU’s 32-24 loss to Ole Miss on September 19. Before that, the 6-foot-7 tight end had become one of Leavitt’s most reliable targets. He had 14 catches for 222 yards and a touchdown through three games, giving the new LSU quarterback a player he could turn to when a play became difficult.Kiffin explained the connection on The Lane Kiffin Show. “TDZ really was the quarterback’s comfort zone,” he said. The LSU coach added that Leavitt often looked for Green on big third downs and made quick, in-rhythm throws to him.That absence was clear against Texas A&M, but LSU found other answers. Jackson Harris had six catches for 163 yards and two touchdowns, including a 57-yard score. Winston Watkins Jr. also finished with five catches for 107 yards. LSU’s official game report confirmed those numbers after the Tigers improved to 3-1.The bigger surprise was Leavitt’s performance. After hurting his right hamstring while running, he could not rely on his legs in the same way. Instead, he stayed in the pocket and attacked through the air. The official LSU report lists him at 17-of-23 passing for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interception.For Kiffin, Harris and Watkins stepping up matters because Green’s absence changes how Leavitt reads key downs. LSU now needs that production to continue.Sam Leavitt injury adds to LSU’s growing concernsKiffin said he was preparing to remove Leavitt from the game after the injury became worse, but the quarterback refused to leave. “He was going to play through it,” Kiffin said, according to LSU coverage of his postgame comments.The injury also created a strange benefit. Louisiana Sports reported that Kiffin joked the hamstring issue may have helped Leavitt because he knew he could not escape the pocket and therefore had to throw on time. That approach worked against Texas A&M, although LSU now has to decide how much it wants to use its starting quarterback against McNeese State.The Tigers have already lost several important players. Safety Dashawn Spears is out for the season with an ACL injury, while wide receiver Phillip Wright III is also out for the year. Linebacker Whit Weeks suffered a serious leg injury against Texas A&M, adding to the pressure on LSU’s depth.LSU hosts McNeese State on October 3 before traveling to Kentucky on October 10. Kiffin has not committed to resting Leavitt, but Louisiana Sports reported that the coach was considering how to handle key players after the recent injuries.Green’s absence remains a separate problem for the offense. LSU needs other receivers and tight ends to keep giving Leavitt reliable targets while he waits to get his most trusted option back.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: J.J. Watt and Kealia Watt’s growing sports empire: From a Burnley FC investment to $7.8 million in youth sports funding across 999 schools
articles.summary: J.J. Watt and Kealia Watt have found a way to keep sports at the center of their lives even after stepping away from professional competition. J.J.
articles.body: J.J. Watt and Kealia Watt have found a way to keep sports at the center of their lives even after stepping away from professional competition. J.J. finished his NFL career as a three-time Defensive Player of the Year and one of the most recognizable defensive players of his generation, while Kealia built her own career in professional soccer and earned three appearances for the U.S. women’s national team. Today, the couple’s influence stretches from English football ownership to television and, most importantly, a charitable foundation that has funded millions of dollars in youth sports programs. Their story is not simply about what two former athletes did with their money after retirement. It is about how they turned their experience, reputation and love for sport into something with a much wider reach.How did J.J. and Kealia Watt move from professional athletes to sports owners?J.J. Watt had already spent years thinking about what would come after football before he retired from the NFL following the 2022 season. After 12 seasons with the Houston Texans and Arizona Cardinals, he had become a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and finished his career with 114.5 sacks. But retirement did not mean leaving professional sports behind.In May 2023, J.J. and Kealia announced that they had become minority investors in Burnley FC, the historic English club based in Lancashire. The investment came just after Burnley won the EFL Championship and secured promotion to the Premier League. The exact size of the couple’s stake and the amount they invested have not been publicly disclosed.For J.J., the move combined two interests. He had followed the Premier League for years, while Kealia brought her own professional soccer background to the decision. The couple had reportedly spent around three years looking for a club they could invest in together before choosing Burnley. J.J. also spoke with Ryan Reynolds about his experience with Wrexham, as the Watts considered how sports ownership could connect them with fans outside the United States.Their approach to Burnley has also been noticeably hands-on. Instead of treating the investment as simply another name on an ownership list, the couple spent time learning about the town, its history and its supporters. J.J. even joined fans at local pubs and community events as he tried to understand what Burnley meant to the people who had supported the club for generations.What are J.J. and Kealia Watt trying to build at Burnley?The Watts have been open about wanting to help Burnley reach more fans internationally, particularly in the United States. But they have also stressed that international growth should not come at the expense of the club’s identity.That balance is important because Burnley is not a new sports brand looking for an audience. The club dates back to 1882 and is deeply connected to the town. When the Watts announced their investment, they described themselves as investing not only in the squad and manager but also in the community around the club.Kealia’s involvement brings another dimension. Having played in the National Women’s Soccer League and for the U.S. national team, she understands the development of women’s professional soccer from the player’s side. When the couple joined Burnley’s ownership group, she specifically spoke about wanting to help with the growth of the club’s women’s team, drawing on what she had seen happen with the NWSL in the United States.J.J.’s post-NFL career has also moved into broadcasting. He joined CBS Sports as an NFL analyst in 2023, giving him another major platform outside playing football.The Burnley investment therefore fits into a much larger transition. J.J. is no longer earning his influence from sacks and defensive plays, while Kealia is no longer building her profile through goals and appearances. Instead, they are using their experience as athletes, their public profiles and their understanding of sports to take on different roles.How big has the J.J. Watt Foundation become?The most measurable part of J.J. Watt’s legacy away from the NFL may be the Justin J. Watt Foundation.Founded in 2011, the foundation focuses on giving middle-school children access to after-school athletic programs. Its mission is built around more than simply getting children onto a playing field. The organization says its programs are designed to help young people develop accountability, teamwork, leadership, work ethic and perseverance in a safe and supervised environment.The scale has grown considerably. According to the foundation’s current figures, it has funded more than $7.8 million for youth athletic programs across 999 schools in 43 states and Washington, D.C. Its progress page currently lists $7,845,386.25 toward an $8 million funding goal.The money goes toward practical needs that can make a difference for school sports programs. Recent grants have helped schools purchase football equipment, soccer uniforms, wrestling mats, basketball equipment, track gear and other supplies.That makes the foundation’s work particularly easy to measure. Instead of simply announcing a broad commitment to young people, the organization provides funding for things students and schools can actually use.The foundation also has a history that extends beyond its regular youth-sports program.How did J.J. Watt turn a personal charity into a national relief effort?One of the biggest moments in J.J. Watt’s charitable career came after Hurricane Harvey struck Houston in 2017.Watt launched a fundraising campaign to help people affected by the disaster. What began with a target of $200,000 eventually grew into a campaign that raised more than $41 million for relief efforts. The funds were distributed through partner organizations working on the ground rather than simply being folded into the foundation’s normal youth-sports program.The scale of that campaign changed the way many people viewed Watt’s charitable work. He was no longer simply a professional athlete running a foundation. His public profile had become powerful enough to bring enormous attention and donations to a crisis affecting an entire community.Importantly, the Harvey campaign should not be confused with the foundation’s regular youth-athletics funding. The foundation itself explains that the Harvey money was distributed to four partner organizations before it returned its focus to after-school athletic programs.That distinction makes the Watts’ overall story more interesting, not less. articles.title: Tony Romo leaves CBS with about $72 million left on his contract. So what happens to it?
articles.summary: Tony Romo is done at CBS Sports.
articles.body: Tony Romo is done at CBS Sports. The network announced Friday that he will not return as an NFL game analyst after his July arrest on charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated. The official line is that the two sides "mutually agreed to part ways." That's 71 days after his arrest in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Funny how "mutual" always shows up right when someone is leaving.Tony Romo leaves CBS after Milwaukee DWI arrest: the mutual exit, the millions, and the pain storyRomo, 46, was arrested in Milwaukee on July 23 after being seen cutting off drivers on I-43 southbound and passing on the right during rush hour. He got three citations: operating under the influence, open intoxicants in a vehicle, and unsafe passing on the right. Body camera footage shows him telling deputies he was leaving a golf course and going to visit his grandparents. Court records show he was also cited for refusing a test after arrest. Fox 4 Dallas, which cited TMZ Sports and the arrest report, said he told deputies he'd had "zero" drinks and that mini liquor bottles were found in his backpack.CBS put him on leave on July 31. J.J. Watt moved in as lead analyst next to Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson. Watt is staying in that seat.In September, Romo pleaded no contest. Afterward, he said on Instagram that back surgeries from his playing days left him in constant pain. That led to painkiller dependence, he said, and then to leaning too hard on alcohol. In his CBS exit statement, he said he'd take time off before thinking about what comes next.Romo signed a 10-year, $180 million deal with CBS, around $17 million a year, making him the highest-paid NFL analyst. Sportico reports about $72 million was left on that contract. Nobody has said what happens to it. Sportico thinks a settlement is likely, but that's their guess. CBS has not confirmed any money details.Romo joined CBS in 2017, replacing Phil Simms as lead analyst. He went from Cowboys legend (four Pro Bowls, franchise leader with 248 touchdown passes) to the face of the network's NFL coverage. Now he's gone in under three months.His pain story is real and deserves respect. But it doesn't erase a refused test, an open container, and a no contest plea. Both things can be true. The question is how much grace someone gets when they're famous, rich, and well-liked. Watt will continue as CBS’s lead NFL analyst for the rest of the 2026 season.Tony Romo breaks silence after CBS Sports departureCBS Sports announced that it and Romo had “mutually agreed to part ways” after his long run with the network. Romo joined CBS in 2017 after retiring from the NFL and quickly became the network’s lead NFL game analyst alongside Jim Nantz. CBS thanked him for his work over the past nine years and wished him well.Romo also shared a statement about the decision, making it clear that he is not rushing into his next job.“I’m proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years. I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life with a desire to win and be the best that I can be,” Romo said.He then explained what he plans to do now.“I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity,” Romo said.The statement comes after a difficult period for the former quarterback. Romo was arrested in Wisconsin on July 23 after a traffic stop and was later placed on leave by CBS Sports. He pleaded no contest to an operating while intoxicated charge on September 1.According to NFL.com, Romo received a six month suspension of his driving privileges, an alcohol assessment requirement and an $834 payment as part of the case.Tony Romo’s CBS Sports exit leaves J.J. articles.title: "I'm not sure anyone has ever asked me this": Matthew Stafford's wife, Kelly Stafford, opens up about football season
articles.summary: Kelly Stafford was asked a simple question on Instagram, and she gave an honest answer. A follower asked how she is doing this football season.
articles.body: Kelly Stafford was asked a simple question on Instagram, and she gave an honest answer. A follower asked how she is doing this football season. She said she wasn't sure anyone had ever asked her that before. Then she said it: it's a lot.Kelly, wife of Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, shared the answer on her Instagram Story. She said she is “stressed often and always planning for the next game, whether that means hosting or getting her girls to another stadium. The rest of her week is kids' sports, homework, and tests. She said she's sure all moms feel the same stress.”Her twist: "I just also have a husband running for his life on Sundays 🤣."Cheeky, yes. But the joke has a lot of truth in it.From Booed in Detroit to Stepping Away From Her Podcast: Kelly Stafford's Real Talk on NFL LifeMatthew is entering his 18th NFL season, his sixth with the Rams, and the couple are raising four daughters. The girls are reportedly between six and nine years old. When Matthew leaves for camp and the season, Kelly runs the home side of things. She has also built her own career as host of the podcast The Morning After with Kelly Stafford.Over the summer, Kelly reportedly said on another podcast that the hardest part for Matthew is missing his kids' weekend sports. That has added to talk that this could be his last season, though nothing is confirmed.She has said this before. This isn't a one-off. Kelly has been open about the pressure for years.In January 2024, Kelly said she and her kids were booed on the sideline before the Lions-Rams wild-card game in Detroit, and that Hunter cried. She said she could handle the boos herself, but felt differently with her girls beside her.Two of her daughters were hospitalized before the Rams' wild-card game against the Vikings, in January 2025, just days after the family evacuated their Los Angeles home because of wildfires. Kelly took the girls to Waffle House afterward and said they were happy to be on dad's work trip.In October 2025, Kelly announced she was stepping back from her own podcast for four weeks to protect her mental health and think about the show's future. She later extended the break to focus on her family and Matthew's season. In a later Q&A, she said she didn't miss the anxiety of waiting to see what headline an episode would create. She said she needed a mental break.Earlier this year, after a tight Rams playoff win, her phone showed 103 missed calls, and she asked if anyone else felt the stress of these games was shaving years off their life. She said on her podcast that the time around Matthew's move was very stressful, and that he is very good at compartmentalizing.Kelly's biggest scare had nothing to do with football. She announced a brain tumor in April 2019 and had a 12-hour surgery two weeks later. She welcomed the couple's fourth child in June 2020. So when she says "it's a lot," she knows what the real hard stuff looks like.The thing is, that nobody asks the person standing on the sideline how she is. Fans ask about the quarterback's arm, his knee, his contract. The wife gets a camera shot in the suite, a nice outfit, and a caption about "supporting her man." The truth is that she's doing a second full-time job without a salary, a stat line, or a highlight reel.Kelly's answer is worth reading because it isn't dramatic. She doesn't complain about her husband or her life. She just says the load is heavy, that it feels like what every mom carries, and then makes a joke because that's how tired people survive. That mix of honest and funny is why her posts travel.It also shows how rare it is for someone to ask. When a woman says "wow, I'm not sure anyone has ever asked me that," it shouldn't be a throwaway line. It should make the rest of us ask more often.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price 'Re-Aggravated' Injury, Ruled Out Week 4
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks will be without rookie running back Jadarian Price for Week 4.
articles.body: The Seattle Seahawks' running back depth chart continues to thin out. On Friday, the Seahawks ruled out rookie Jadarian Price ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. Price, according to head coach Mike Macdonald, "re-aggravated" a chest injury that he originally sustained when the Seahawks played the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2. Coming off a 33-31 loss in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders, Price's absence puts the Seahawks in a further bind at a position they were already struggling at. The Seahawks have been without veteran running back Zach Charbonnet, who entered the 2026 season on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list after tearing his ACL during the NFC Divisional Round last season. Charbonnet returned to practice on Thursday, meaning his return could be near, but he's required to miss at least four games, which includes this upcoming week. Depth hasn't been the only issue with the Seahawks running back position. Price was selected 32nd overall in the 2026 NFL Draft, with the intention of filling the void left by Kenneth Walker, the 2026 Super Bowl MVP who signed with the Kansas City Chiefs in the offseason. Instead, the Notre Dame product has struggled in his first three NFL games. Price has gained 119 yards on 28 carries, has not reached the end zone, and lost a costly fumble in the Seahawks' defeat last week. Now, Price's development will be halted as he recovers from this lingering injury. In his place, Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani will carry the load for the Seahawks ground attack during Sunday's 4:25 p.m. matchup with the Chargers.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy sees Giants as 'an opportunity' after shock trade from Vikings
articles.summary: New Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy spoke for the first time after his trade from the Vikings and talked about how he sees his new home as an opportunity.
articles.body:
A few days after the Giants traded for quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the young gunslinger made his first public comments to the media following Friday's practice.

Speaking in the locker room, the 23-year-old said "it was a shock" when he was traded by the Vikings, the team that drafted him No. 10 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft.

Although his first two seasons with Minnesota didn't go as planned, McCarthy understood the business of the NFL and after the initial shock, is taking the move in stride.

"It's been a whirlwind, the full experience of the nature of the beast, which is the NFL," he told the media including the Daily News' Pat Leonard . "But I'm extremely grateful for all the time in Minnesota. So many great relationships. So many learning lessons and growth. And I'm just so fired up to be a New York Football Giant."

McCarthy said he didn't see the move coming, but sees his move to New York as an opportunity.

"At the end of the day, it's an opportunity," he said. "An opportunity to take advantage of."

The Giants were in need of a quarterback after losing Jaxson Dart for the regular season. Jameis Winston , who will start the team's Week 4 matchup with the Cardinals, is a veteran capable of starting, but has struggled offensively in parts of the last two weeks. McCarthy will give the Giants another capable quarterback who has started in this league, while also evaluating what the Michigan product can bring to the team.

Coach John Harbaugh and the rest of the staff have eased McCarthy into the offense , and they thought he did a good job with what they asked him to do this week at practice.

"He practiced the things we asked him to do. Had different things for him, here and there. A lot of it is learning the offense," Harbaugh said Friday. "Thought he did a good job with that; 24/7 almost, really. Trying to be immersed in the offense. He wants to learn it, he wants to know it all. That's what we've been working on. It's kind of what you expect."

The team has yet to announce the QB pecking order for this week. It's safe to assume Winston will start, with Jake Haener in the mix to be the team's backup, but Harbaugh, as to be expected, did not divulge the plan.

"We're not announcing any of that right now," Harbaugh said. "And I would say probably, honestly, we're probably still figuring it out. What exactly, how do we use him [McCarthy]? How do we use Jake in those kinds of backup roles? Who's ready for what? Jake's only been here for like a month, too. But he's obviously more immersed in the offense. So we have to decide those things."

However the Giants depth chart looks this Sunday, McCarthy is using this fresh start to become acclimated to the offense and his new teammates.

"Being in the league almost over 2.5 years now, who you are is who you are," he said. "I just try to be authentically me, because the locker room's gonna find out eventually. So I just try to be myself and do whatever I can to just be a guy that lets them know that I love this game.

"I'm gonna work my butt off," he said, "and I love these guys around me."

The Giants (2-1) look to continue their winning ways when they host the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday at 1 p.m.

articles.title: Damar Hamlin’s foundation provides new AED to Sto-Rox
articles.summary: A life-saving device is now part of the lineup at Sto-Rox.
articles.body:
A life-saving device is now part of the lineup at Sto-Rox.

The school received an AED from Damar Hamlin's Chasing M's Foundation and the NFL.

Because of a new state law signed this past spring, every school in the PIAA is required to have an automated external defibrillator at every single sporting event.

It hits especially close to home at Sto-Rox with all of the work Buffalo Bills safety Damar Hamlin has done to increase access to AEDs and CPR classes since he went into cardiac arrest on the football field three years ago.

"I got it in the mail. I was like, 'Oh, I seen him in the NFL,' and I lit up. I was like, 'Wow, that's cool,'" Sto-Rox Athletic Director Shomari Phelps said.

Thirty Pennsylvania schools got AEDs during the draft, an initiative that pushed the foundation past $1 million worth of AED donations.

Damar Hamlin's father, Mario Hamlin, said, "It's a full-circle moment for my son, you know, he takes great pride into making sure that he's able to keep the youth safe."

Hamlin tells Channel 11 Sports it's a milestone bigger than football.

"It's just impact on the world I truly never seen myself being able to make, but something that I always wanted to be able to leave behind. A name that will last longer than me. I think being able to save these lives of people that I'll never meet is something that will keep me a household name for a very long time."

Chasing M's also pushes for legislative action, like Greg Moyer's Law in Pennsylvania.

It's the law that mandates AEDs at PIAA games and practices, named for Moyer, who went into cardiac arrest and died at a high school basketball game in 2000.

Sto-Rox already had AED access and training requirements for coaches in place, but Athletic Director Shomari Phelps is happy to see renewed precaution for a new school year.

"To be proactive instead of reactive in those situations. So, I'm glad that you know it is mandated by law, and it's something that we take very seriously here," Phelps said.

It's something Hamlin's foundation hopes will become the standard.

"I'm really hoping that this common sense bill is adopted by all 50 states, and that just the people know that being prepared saves lives," Mario Halmin said.

The American Heart Association says immediate access to AEDs and CPR can double or even triple survival rates.

articles.title: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes’ 1587 lawsuit takes a new turn as Kansas City Chiefs stars continue backing restaurant amid ongoing trademark dispute
articles.summary: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes continue to back 1587 Prime as a trademark lawsuit puts the restaurant’s name under scrutiny.
articles.body: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes continue to back 1587 Prime as a trademark lawsuit puts the restaurant’s name under scrutiny. The Chiefs stars remain publicly connected to the steakhouse, while their lawyers are trying to remove them from the case. The dispute has also raised questions over how much involvement the two players had in creating the restaurant’s identity.Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes continue backing 1587 Prime despite lawsuitThe latest sign of support came through social media. 1587 Prime announced that Yelp had named it one of its Best New Restaurants of 2026. Kelce reshared the restaurant’s Instagram post on his Story with fire emojis, while Mahomes also shared the announcement.The post announced that the restaurant was named one of Yelp’s Best New Restaurants of 2026.“A Prime year, indeed. 1587 Prime has been named one of Yelp’s Best New Restaurants of 2026, a recognition made all the more meaningful by the Kansas City community and its continued support,” the restaurant’s official account wrote on Instagram.For a business facing a trademark dispute, the Yelp mention gives 1587 Prime another piece of positive attention.The name remains at the center of the lawsuit. Mahomes and Kelce launched the restaurant with hospitality group Noble 33, using their Chiefs jersey numbers to create “1587.” Mahomes wears No. 15, while Kelce wears No. 87.1587 Sneakers claims that the restaurant’s use of the number infringes its trademark rights. The company says it began selling shoes in April 2023 and later filed for the “1587” trademark. That application remains under review by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.The restaurant’s parent company had already filed for the “1587 Prime” trademark in December 2023. That application covers bar and restaurant services, while the sneaker company’s filing covers clothing.The difference between those categories could become important as the case develops. Trademark attorney Josh Gerben of Gerben IP, who does not represent either side, discussed the dispute with ESPN.“I think it’s a tough case for the sneaker company,” Gerben said while speaking with ESPN about the trademark fight.Gerben also raised the question of consumer confusion, noting that trademarks can exist across different industries. The issue is now part of the wider disagreement between the two businesses.1587 Sneakers claims that customers have contacted the company believing it had a connection to 1587 Prime. The sneaker company wants the restaurant to stop using the name and selling goods carrying it. It has also requested punitive damages.1587 Sneakers pushes back against Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce’s dismissal bidThe legal fight has also focused directly on the two Chiefs stars. Their lawyers asked the court on July 3 to dismiss all claims against Mahomes and Kelce with prejudice.The players’ legal team argues that neither star controls the restaurant and that they lack ties to New York, where the lawsuit was filed. That argument seeks to separate Mahomes and Kelce from the business beyond their public association with the brand.1587 Sneakers has strongly disputed that position. In its August 4 response, the company argued that Mahomes and Kelce played an active role in creating the “1587” identity because the number comes from their football jersey numbers.The filing called the players “the generative force from which the infringing mark derives its entire identity and market appeal.”The sneaker company also accused the two players of trying to present themselves as little more than promotional figures for the restaurant. Its filing argued that their involvement went beyond simply lending their names to the business.The players have sought dismissal, while 1587 Sneakers wants the claims to continue. The court has not issued a final ruling on the underlying trademark allegations.Currently, 1587 Prime continues operating and Mahomes and Kelce continue promoting the restaurant. articles.title: La NFL sanciona al dueño de los 49ers por su arresto en una operación contra la prostitución
articles.standfirst: Jed York, que reconoce que fue "un error imperdonable", ha sido multado con 500.000 dólares y sancionado con seis partidos
articles.summary: Jed York, que reconoce que fue "un error imperdonable", ha sido multado con 500.000 dólares y sancionado con seis partidos
articles.body: La NFL ha suspendido durante seis partidos a Jed York, propietario de los San Francisco 49ers, por su arresto a principios de año en una operación encubierta contra la prostitución en Ohio. Además, la liga le ha impuesto una multa de 500.000 dólares por incumplir su política de conducta personal. El propietario de la franquicia californiana se declaró culpable y también de posesión de instrumentos delictivos por utilizar su teléfono para responder a un anuncio encubierto de prostitución publicado en internet. Aceptó la sanción y pidió disculpas en un comunicado difundido por los propios 49ers y recogido en varios medios internacionales. York, a través de 49ers Enterprises, también posee participaciones en el Leeds United de la Premier League y en el Rangers escocés. York ha pedido perdón por lo sucedido. "A mi familia, a los jugadores, entrenadores y empleados de los San Francisco 49ers, a nuestros aficionados y socios, les pido disculpas. Fue un error imperdonable y asumo toda la responsabilidad. Lo que hice no refleja mis valores ni el hombre que aspiro a ser para mi familia", dijo. York también reconoció que sus actos no fueron el ejemplo que quiere transmitir a sus hijos. "Ahora espero mostrarles la importancia de reconocer los propios errores y que incluso nuestros peores momentos nos enseñan a ser mejores", añadió. York no ha participado en ningún partido ni reunión de la NFL esta temporada y la liga le ha computado tres de los seis encuentros de sanción. Podrá reincorporarse el próximo 20 de octubre, después del partido que los 49ers disputarán la noche anterior ante Washington. York fue detenido en agosto por el Grupo de Trabajo contra la Trata de Personas del Valle de Mahoning. Según la policía, el propietario de los 49ers intentaba pagar 160 dólares por mantener relaciones sexuales con una mujer a la que creía prostituta. Tras ser detenido, York fue ingresado en prisión y posteriormente puesto en libertad después de abonar una fianza de 5.000 dólares. En un primer momento fue acusado de ser cliente de prostitución, aunque la fiscalía modificó posteriormente el cargo por el de alteración del orden público. Fue condenado a un día de cárcel por ambos delitos y recibió una multa de 1.150 dólares.

articles.title: Week 4 Waiver Wire Top Targets For This Week's Injured Fantasy Football Stars
articles.summary: Week 4 opened with an exciting battle between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns on Thursday night. It will resume with a Sunday morning matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders in London.
articles.body:
Week 4 opened with an exciting battle between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns on Thursday night. It will resume with a Sunday morning matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders in London.

Don't forget to have those Sunday lineups set early, folks.

While managers are looking at a full 16-game schedule this week—the first byes will come in Week 5—they may need to find replacements for several injured stars. While the waiver wire has largely been picked over by the weekend, a few serviceable options should still be available.

Here, we'll dive into the Week 4 injury report , provide rankings for the top remaining plays, and highlight some of those aforementioned late-week targets. All rankings and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

The big question at quarterback this week involves the Chicago Bears. While Caleb Williams has been ruled out, the Bears haven't announced whether Case Keenum will start a second consecutive game or if primary backup Tyson Bagent will take over.

"We'll find out on Sunday," head coach Ben Johnson said, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be without quarterback Baker Mayfield as he's recovering from a dislocated thumb.

Though Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels did make some progress this week, he's been officially ruled out with a dislocated elbow. That means Marcus Mariota will get the start for Washington, and both he and Daniel Jones could shine in Sunday morning's matchup.

Mariota threw a trio of touchdown passes against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3. Washington's defense, meanwhile, has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season. Mariota and Jones are rostered in 13 percent and 24 percent of fantasy leagues, respectively.

Kirk Cousins, Geno Smith, and Michael Penix Jr. are other potential late-week adds at quarterback.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

The Commanders have also ruled out running back Rachaad White, while the New York Jets have ruled out Breece Hall. Tennessee Titans running back Tyjae Spears is listed as questionable.

The Miami Dolphins placed De'Von Achane on injured reserve with a torn ACL this past week. This makes Ollie Gordon II a prime waiver wire pickup, even though he has a tough matchup against the Vikings this week.

Gordon projects as Miami's new starter and is still available in roughly a third of fantasy leagues. Fellow Dolphins back Jaylen Wright is only rostered in 28 percent of leagues and could have real value if Miami utilizes a committee approach.

Las Vegas Raiders running back Mike Washington Jr. has a lot of upside as a complement to Ashton Jeanty, and he's a top option for managers not willing to bank on Miami. He had five carries for 54 yards and a touchdown last week, and he's still only rostered in 40 percent of leagues.

The big news at receiver this week is the fact that the Minnesota Vikings have ruled out Justin Jefferson with an ankle injury. The Philadelphia Eagles have also ruled out DeVonta Smith and Marquise Brown.

Xavier Legette, Caleb Douglas, and Colbie Young are also out. The list of receivers listed as questionable includes Mike Evans, Zay Flowers, Ladd McConkey, Terry McLaurin, and Jalen Coker.

With Alec Pierce on injured reserve, Colts receiver Keenan Allen is a veritable must-add this week, even though he's questionable for Week 4. He's coming off a six-catch, 63-yard, one-touchdown performance and has a tremendous matchup against Washington on Sunday.

The Commanders have surrendered an average of 39 fantasy points to opposing receiver groups this season. If Allen can't go, he's worth stashing for the next couple of weeks, and Darius Slayton could have Week 4 value.

Slayton hasn't suited up for the Colts yet this year, and he's rostered in only one percent of fantasy leagues.

With Smith and Brown out, Eagles receivers Makai Lemon and Dontayvion Wicks are both sensible pickups, though their ceilings are probably limited. Rashod Bateman, Wan'Dale Robinson, and Mack Hollins are other WRs to consider adding off the wire this week.

49ers Owner Jed York Suspended 6 Games (AP)

The Eagles have ruled out tight end Dallas Goedert, while the Los Angeles Chargers have ruled out Charlie Kolar.

It's worth checking to see if Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq is still available, even though he's questionable this week, as he's rostered in 54 percent of leagues.

Sadiq is coming off a seven-catch, 105-yard, one-touchdown outing, and he'll have multiple opportunities against the Bears on Sunday. With Hall, Mitchell, and fellow tight end Mason Taylor out, Sadiq should be a big part of the offensive game plan.

Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller, who is rostered in 32 percent of leagues, is another premium pickup this week. He'll face a Detroit Lions defense that has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing tight ends than any other team.

T.J. Hockenson, Brenton Strange, and AJ Barner are other tight ends to consider on the wire this week.

articles.title: Mike Evans Injury Update: 49ers WR Playing Through “Pretty Painful” Injury
articles.summary: Mike Evans suffered a rib injury midway through Week 3's shootout against the Arizona Cardinals, but it might not keep him from suiting up in Week 4. Origina...
articles.body:
Mike Evans suffered a rib injury midway through Week 3's shootout against the Arizona Cardinals, but it might not keep him from suiting up in Week 4. Originally entering the league as a first-round pick in the 2014 NFL Draft , Evans spent most of his career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and established himself as one of the game's most consistent threats on the perimeter and in the red zone. Recording at least 1,000 yards in his first 11 seasons, Evans battled injury in 2025 and joined the San Francisco 49ers in the offseason.

While he left Sunday's contest early with an injury, it sounds like pain tolerance will ultimately decide if he can play against the Denver Broncos. In a recent tweet, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said that Mike Evans is intends to play through a "pretty painful" rib injury. While nothing is confirmed, this language suggests the potential Hall of Famer will suit up for the team's Week 4 showdown with Denver.

Mike Evans Injury Update: 49ers Star WR Questionable With "Pretty Painful" Rib Injury

Mike Evans is no longer the dominant player he was in the 2010s and early 2020s, but he has played pretty well for the 49ers thus far. In Week 1, the veteran finished the night with a respectable six receptions for 49 yards and a touchdown on seven targets against a strong Los Angeles Rams defense. He was off to a similar start in Week 2, recording three receptions for 54 yards before suffering a hip injury. He had three receptions for 34 yards and a touchdown in Week 3 before the rib injury sidelined him.

Based on Rapoport's tweet, it's likely that Mike Evans will suit up for the team's Week 4 battle against the Denver Broncos. At 2-1, the Broncos look like one of the better teams in the AFC, and they need to keep winning to keep pace with the 3-0 Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders. San Francisco, meanwhile, holds a one-game lead in the NFC West over the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: Cowboys Joey Porter Jr. Trade: Was It Worth It?
articles.summary: The shocking news came down Thursday night of the Cowboys’ Joey Porter Jr. trade. The Dallas Cowboys traded for the Pittsburgh Steelers’ young star cornerbac...
articles.body:
The shocking news came down Thursday night of the Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. trade. The Dallas Cowboys traded for the Pittsburgh Steelers' young star cornerback Porter Jr. In the trade, Dallas sent away a 2028 second-round pick and a sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft.

It became increasingly likely that Porter Jr. and the Steelers couldn't agree to a long-term contract extension. The Cowboys were one of the few teams heavily linked to the defensive back. Now that the deal is official, the question is: is it worth it for Dallas?

Cowboys Joey Porter Jr. Trade: Porter Jr. Gives The Cowboys A Long-Term Answer At Cornerback

The Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. trade isn't for a veteran cornerback who may only have one or two years left before he falls off. Porter Jr. not only gives Dallas immediate help at corner but for the foreseeable future as well.

​Typically in moves like the Cowboys Joey Porter Jr. trade, it gets revealed minutes after the initial deal announcement that the player that got moved has signed a long-term extension. Yet this isn't the case here, as it's been announced that Porter Jr. will play the rest of this season on the final year of his rookie contract.

​Pittsburgh's former second-round pick is only 26 years old and coming off the best year of his career. This past season, in man coverage, amongst all cornerbacks who faced at least 30 man coverage targets. Porter Jr. allowed a mere 35.3% completion percentage; this mark was the lowest in the NFL, per Pro Football Focus .

​​Porter Jr. in the 2025 season finished 11th best in catch rate allowed at 11%. He allowed a career-best passer rating allowed of 66.8, ranking third in the NFL this season. ​Pro Football Focus graded Porter Jr. with a 76.6 coverage grade; not only was it the best of his career, but he ranked 13th among all qualified cornerbacks. He also tied for the fourth-highest pass breakups in the NFL with 13.

Cowboys Joey Porter Jr. Trade: Cowboys Secondary Has Been A Consistent Problem

Dallas's secondary has not been good, to put it nicely, so far in 2026; they've allowed an EPA per pass of 0.37. This ranks tied for 31st in the NFL with the Arizona Cardinals and only ahead of the Miami Dolphins. The Cowboys' porous secondary being in the same vicinity of two teams who are in rebuilding mode is certainly not good, to say the least. These secondary issues, though, date back even to last season, as they ranked 31st in EPA per pass with a 0.13 finish.

Dallas has an offense good enough to be a contender, as it ranks top seven in EPA per play, success%, and EPA per pass going into week four. The defense, though, hasn't been able to hold its own weight. The Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. trade, by addressing the leaky secondary, can change that.

What's your take? Post it in our free sports community at stadiumrant.app , or download Stadium Rant on the App Store.

End Of My Cowboys Joey Porter Jr. Trade Rant

Dallas fired Matt Eberflus this past offseason and hired Christian Parker to be their new defensive coordinator. After the first three weeks of the defense under Parker's direction getting off to a rocky start, the Cowboys went out and gave him a new piece for his chessboard.

Porter Jr. comes in and is without a question the best cornerback on the Dallas roster. Now it's up to Parker to utilize the corner in the correct way and Porter Jr. to live up to his billing.

articles.title: The Browns in the playoffs? Not so fast
articles.summary: Everyone, slow your roll, the Cleveland Browns are 3-1 but NFL playoff talk is a bit early.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns find themselves at 3-1-0 in this young 2026 season. Three comeback wins have been featured so far and show that Cleveland has no quit.

The win over division rival Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football placed the Browns in first place all alone atop the AFC North Division.

And that is all well and good. Everyone wants to win games and become fans of something they feel is relevant. It is easier to root for a team that is winning games than to be devoted to a club that continually rests in the basement on an annual basis.

With the win, certainly Cleveland will obviously climb in the league power rankings. The league has five undefeated teams going into Week 4, and nine teams that are currently at 2-1-0 that could improve their standing once the smoke from the weekend subsides.

Teams that begin their season 3-1-0 have made the playoffs 75% of the time since the NFL expanded its postseason format in 2020. Remember, the consensus for the Browns before the year began was a five-win season, six at most?

It is a distinct possibility that Cleveland could be ranked in the Top 10. No, really. There are a few media outlets that are predicting a playoff spot for the Browns. So are numerous Facebook fan pages. Really? Let's slow this down a bit and be more realistic.

Jacob Robinson of The Athletic said this about Cleveland's sudden ascension:

"What about surprise 3-1 teams like these Browns? Projected before the season to win five games, Cleveland had Super Bowl odds of +15000, ranking 28th at the time. This start is very different from most."

For one, it's just one win. A key division matchup, to be certain, but simply one game on the schedule. There are 13 remaining.

Cleveland has beaten the 1-2-0 Carolina Panthers, the 0-3-0 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the now 2-2-0 Steelers. Nothing in this grouping screams potential Super Bowl champion. The only good team they faced was the Jacksonville Jaguars, who took Cleveland to the wood shed to the tune of a 34-10 beatdown.

There is a saying: "It's not what you are, but who you've played."

Now, don't get this all wrong; the Browns have the opportunity to gain double-digit wins this year. No, really. Because they were at the bottom of the division last year, they are set up with what is called "the fourth-place schedule" this year. That means they are pitted against the majority of clubs that also finished dead last in their division in 2025. Playing last year's crappy teams is a wonderful thing.

On the schedule are the New York Jets, New Orleans Saints, Tennessee Titans, Las Vegas Raiders, Indianapolis Colts, New York Football Giants, and Atlanta Falcons. Seven wins from this group? Six? Even five victories place Cleveland at eight wins for the year. With seven playoff seeds in the AFC, getting into the postseason will require a minimum of 10 wins. 11 gets you in.

But hold the phone. The Houston Texans were expected to be in the AFC Championship Game this year, and yet currently are 0-3-0. The Browns play Houston in Week 10. If Cleveland can split with every team in the division, that is another three wins. The victory over Pittsburgh is a direct indication that this could happen.

The Browns are the only team in the division that has never won an AFC North Division crown. Back in the day, they captured the AFC Central many times, but so far, since the realignment, they have never won the division title now called the AFC North. This could happen. This year.

And the playoffs could happen as well. Then again, the bottom could fall out. Lord knows the team collects penalties and allows a team like the Steelers to crawl back into the game after building a big lead.

"Should we trust Cleveland? Naturally, fans are concerned. These Browns are also different in another way, as they're 3-1 despite having a negative points margin (minus-14) on the season. But there's good news there, too. The recent history of 3-1 teams with negative differentials is a reminder that a winning record is all you need."

Last year, the Arizona Cardinals began their season 2-0-0, and everyone started talking playoffs. The Cardinals are a 127-year franchise, and they ended their season 3-14-0. It was the greatest number of losses in a single season in team history. Yet, they began on top of the world.

Let's just enjoy the moment. When the Browns begin beating the really good NFL teams, like the Baltimore Ravens, then let's start discussing the postseason.

What would you put the odds of the Browns making the NFL playoffs this year?

articles.title: Puka Nacua Injury Update: Rams WR “Will Play” In Week 4
articles.summary: Puka Nacua missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to injury, and the latest report reveals he will return to the field in Week 4. Originally selected in the fifth round of...
articles.body:
Puka Nacua missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to injury, and the latest report reveals he will return to the field in Week 4. Originally selected in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft , the BYU product quickly became one of the biggest draft steals in recent memory. Developing an immediate connection with quarterback Matthew Stafford, the rookie finished his inaugural campaign with 105 receptions for 1,486 yards and six touchdowns on 160 targets. While injuries limited him to just 11 games in 2024, he bounced back in 2025 by recording a league-best 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns. He made the second Pro Bowl of his career and earned First-Team All-Pro honors for his work.

There is no denying that Puka Nacua is one of the game's best receivers, and it sounds like the Rams will have him on the field when they face the 2-1 Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. According to ESPN's Sarah Barshop , the wide receiver "will play," but he could be on a snap count.

Puka Nacua Injury Update: Rams WR "Will Play," Could Be On Snap Count

Needless to say, the Los Angeles Rams are at their best when Puka Nacua is on the field. Placing him on a snap count isn't an ideal situation, but the fact he's on the field at all suggests he will suit up for Week 4.

While the offense wasn't the primary issue in the team's 30-26 Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos, Nacua's availability probably was the difference in this contest. At 1-2, Los Angeles currently finds themselves tied for last in what is arguably the most competitive division in football. This team should still make the playoffs, but this early hole could keep them from winning the division.

With Puka Nacua sidelined the past two weeks, most of the offense went through Davante Adams. The veteran finished Week 2 with eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns and followed it up with seven receptions for 137 yards in Week 3. Assuming Nacua plays, Adams will likely take more of a backseat but should still be a key part of the passing attack.
