articles.title: Panthers vs Lions: 5 Questions with Pride of Detroit
articles.summary: Get the Detroit-style view of Week 4's game
articles.body:
Week 4 of the young 2026 NFL season already has the Carolina Panthers and Detroit Lions trending in different directions. The Lions are playoff contenders and quiet Super Bowl hopefuls. Your 2025 NFC South champions, on the other hand, are just hoping that there are fewer injuries in the 13 weeks after their Week 5 bye than there were in the four weeks prior to it.

That doesn't mean that Lions fans are taking this week for granted or that the Lions themselves haven't struggled with their more fair share of inuries. Ryan Matthews from Pride of Detroit answered five of my questions about the Lions to try to give us their side of this story. These answers were the sober, attentive reflections of a fan whose team has only very recently known success, at least relative to their history. In short, they did not fill me with confidence and optimism in the Panthers chances of catching Detroit in the midst of a cat nap.

The Carolina Panthers are quite literally half the team they expected to be when they started training camp. How are the Lions faring with the injury bug this deep into the 2026 season?

The Lions' 2026 roster has bites going back to 2025 that have really put them in a bind on the backend of their defense. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch, once considered to be the top safety duo in the NFL, suffered season-ending injuries last season, and they're still on the PUP heading into this Week 4 matchup. Detroit's secondary has been lit up three straight weeks in a row, and while the cornerbacks haven't been playing their best ball, missing both Joseph and Branch in their respective safety positions has made for some tough viewing when the Lions defense takes the field.

Avonte Maddox, a veteran defensive back, was re-signed to compete for a spot in Detroit's secondary. He earned it in the summer. Maddox played some free safety, box safety, and in the slot as a nickelback to start the season, but he suffered an injury in Week 2 that put him on injured reserve for the foreseeable future. Thomas Harper is another player who played his way into a spot in the secondary, but he, too, suffered an ankle injury in Week 2's game against Buffalo that put him on IR as well. That leaves Chuck Clark, a veteran on his fourth stop in as many seasons, to hold down the single-high safety looks for the most part, and safeties coach Jim O'Neil trusts him in that role. Alongside him is Christian Izien, a player who looked like he was shot out of a cannon in his season debut last week against the Jets. Izien had a groin injury crop up at the end of training camp, but he's a guy who many expected to play the Branch role: box safety, in the slot, up near the line of scrimmage. Izien led the Lions in tackles (11) and finished second in defensive stops (4) against the Jets in Week 3.

Unfortunately—or fortunately depending on how you're looking at it—Panthers fans won't get to see the return of Cade Mays this weekend in Carolina after he had a freak wrist injury near the beginning of camp. Otherwise, the Lions have been pretty fortunate with injuries!

The Lions are already on their second offensive coordinator since Ben Johnson left for the Chicago Bears. What are your hopes and worries three games into the Drew Petzing era?

For all the "Dan Campbell is a Ben Johnson merchant" and "Detroit sure misses Ben Johnson" talk, Drew Petzing's offense has hung 31 points in three consecutive weeks. After a bit of a slow start in terms of opening drives and third-down efficiency, the early returns on Petzing are pretty promising. Jared Goff looks comfortable in the offense, getting into favorable checks and commanding the group. The offensive line dealt with some injuries in the first couple of weeks to their starting left guard—Christian Mahogany—and starting right tackle—rookie Blake Miller—but they looked like a really solid and steady unit when they returned in Week 3.

Some mild concerns for me, and they're admittedly a bit nitpicky, are play calls near the goal line. Last week, nearing the end of the half and the Jets with just one timeout remaining, Detroit called a designed rollout for Goff on first down that he effectively threw away and a fade route to Amon-Ra St. Brown that did result in a touchdown. It left the Jets with 1:36 on the clock and a timeout still at their disposal, but would've liked to see the Lions get to their bread and butter by running the football, forcing the Jets to burn their timeout, and playing with their aggressive, four-down approach on offense. Which seems to run counterintuitive to my second nitpick about the offense: the number of run plays on second-and-10. Petzing's explanation referred back to Detroit's four-down approach on offense, but against the Bills, it felt like Buffalo knew it was coming, but Detroit still stuck with it, leaving them in plenty of third-and-long situations.

Again, early results are trending in a positive way, those concerns are mild at most, but the Lions feel like they're in a much better spot on offense than they were a season ago.

What's with barely beating the Saints and the Jets? I thought y'all were supposed to be a good team.

Is the suggestion here that the Saints and Jets aren't good football teams? Because New Orleans went into Baltimore and took home a victory, and then they nearly pulled out last week's game against a 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders team. The Jets are some clock mismanagement away from being a 2-1 football team themselves, so I think Detroit has actually played some pretty tough teams that will challenge for the playoffs in their respective conferences.

A rain game where one team is looking to establish a struggling rushing attack against another team that surrendered almost 300 yards in their last home game doesn't sound like a good time. Any chance Jahmyr Gibbs is on vacation or enough of a Wizard of Oz style witch where he isn't allowed to get wet?

Jahmyr Gibbs figures to be available come rain, sleet, snow, or such poor field conditions that the NFLPA has to file a grievance .

You're going to predict a Lions win, there's no doubt or shame in that. The interesting question is how big of a win do you think the Lions will have and does that differ from the expectations of the broader Lions fanbase?

There's no way Dan Campbell will have this Lions team overlooking this Panthers team, and I'm not going to either. Their passing attack is explosive, their run defense against running backs has actually been pretty solid the past two weeks, and they're likely getting Devin Lloyd back for this one. While this one could very well become a shootout—weather permitting—it should be a more tightly contested game. It wouldn't surprise me if the Lions win by less than one score, and it wouldn't shock me if the Panthers pull off the upset as home underdogs coming off a disappointing loss in Week 3.

articles.title: A look back at the Colts’ international game history
articles.summary: The Colts return to London in Week 4 after previous regular-season trips to London, Frankfurt and Berlin.
articles.body:
Indianapolis will face the Washington Commanders in London in Week 4, marking the franchise's fourth regular-season international game and its third trip overseas in the last four seasons. What once felt like a rare event has quietly become a fairly regular part of the Colts' schedule.

The franchise has played internationally before in the preseason, including a 2005 American Bowl matchup against the Falcons in Tokyo, but the more interesting history begins with the regular-season games. The Colts have already played in London, Frankfurt and Berlin, and they enter this weekend with a 2-1 record outside the United States.

Here is a look back at how those regular season games played out before Indianapolis returns to London.

The Colts' first regular-season international game came in 2016 against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium.

Indianapolis fell behind 23-6 before making a late push, scoring three touchdowns in the fourth quarter and getting within three points. Andrew Luck threw for 234 yards and two touchdowns, but the comeback fell short as Jacksonville held on for a 30-27 win.

It was also an AFC South game, which made the stakes a little different from the usual international matchup. The Colts were technically the road team and left London at 1-3 after a frustrating start to the season.

The NFL's international operation was still much smaller at the time. London games were becoming more common, but Germany had yet to enter the rotation and the league had not expanded its overseas schedule anywhere close to what it looks like today.

For the Colts, it was their first taste of regular-season football abroad, and it ended with a loss.

Seven years later, the Colts finally returned overseas, this time to Germany.

The result was much better, even if the football itself was not particularly memorable.

Indianapolis beat New England 10-6 in Frankfurt in one of the stranger games of the 2023 season. Gardner Minshew threw for only 194 yards, the Colts scored one touchdown and the two teams combined for just 16 points.

Jonathan Taylor scored Indianapolis' only touchdown, while the defense did most of the work. The Colts intercepted Mac Jones late in the fourth quarter before New England eventually turned to Bailey Zappe for its final possession.

It was not pretty, but nobody asks how an international win looks afterward.

The victory gave the Colts their first regular-season win outside the United States and evened their international record at 1-1.

2025: Colts 31, Falcons 25 (OT) — Berlin

The Colts did not have to wait another seven years for their next trip.

Indianapolis faced Atlanta in Berlin last season, playing in the first NFL regular-season game ever held in the German capital. Unlike the previous two international games, the Colts were the designated home team.

This one was easily the most entertaining of the three.

The game went to overtime tied at 25 before Indianapolis finished it with a touchdown to earn a 31-25 victory. The win improved the Colts to 2-1 internationally and gave them consecutive victories in Germany after the 2023 win in Frankfurt.

It was also part of what has become a much larger NFL push into Europe. Germany has quickly become one of the league's biggest international markets, and the Colts have now been involved in games in two different German cities.

For a franchise that went seven years between its first and second regular-season international appearances, the trips have suddenly started piling up.

If the previous three trips are any indication, expecting another close game would make sense. Every Colts regular-season international game has been decided by six points or fewer. They lost 30-27 to Jacksonville in 2016, beat New England 10-6 in Frankfurt and needed overtime to beat Atlanta 31-25 in Berlin last season.

The settings have changed, the opponents have changed and the quality of football has certainly varied, but the Colts have never had an easy afternoon overseas. Even the 2023 Patriots game, which was not exactly an offensive showcase, stayed undecided until the final minutes.

There is also an element of unpredictability that comes with these games. The travel schedule is different, the routine during the week changes and both teams are playing in an environment they do not normally experience during the season. That does not automatically make every international game close, but the Colts' history suggests they have rarely been comfortable either way.

Indianapolis comes into this one trying to build off its win over Houston after an 0-2 start, so another one-score game would hardly be surprising. The Colts have already played two tight games in the last two weeks, and their international history has followed the same pattern.

Ten years after their first London trip, the Colts are back in England with a 2-1 regular-season international record and a chance to make it three straight wins overseas. Based on how their previous trips have gone, they may have to sweat through another one to get there.

articles.title: "Unpredictability and unreliability": The real reason behind Tony Romo’s CBS exit? Network reportedly wanted freedom from $180M deal before arrest
articles.summary: Tony Romo’s nine-year run with CBS Sports is over, but the latest reporting suggests his July OWI arrest was not the full story behind the split.
articles.body: Tony Romo’s nine-year run with CBS Sports is over, but the latest reporting suggests his July OWI arrest was not the full story behind the split. CBS and Romo announced Friday that they had mutually agreed to part ways, ending his time as the network’s lead NFL analyst. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback had four years and about $72 million left on the 10-year, $180 million deal he signed in 2020. According to The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand, CBS had concerns about Romo’s work and reliability before the arrest. The legal trouble, his reporting suggests, gave the network a reason to finally make a change.Why did CBS reportedly want out of Tony Romo’s contract?Marchand’s reporting points to problems that went beyond what happened in Milwaukee. He wrote that CBS wanted to “break free” of Romo’s contract because of concerns about his “unpredictability, lack of preparation, and unreliability.” His sources also told him Romo “didn’t work hard enough as a broadcaster” and “the further he got away from playing, the less he knew. He didn’t study and failed to learn new players and schemes.”Those are reported criticisms, not findings from CBS itself. Still, they add context to a relationship that had already become more complicated after Romo’s fast start in the booth.Romo joined CBS immediately after retiring from the NFL in 2017 and quickly built a reputation for predicting plays before they happened. That success helped lead to the huge 2020 extension. But according to Marchand, CBS executives had already discussed Romo’s broadcasting work with him before Super Bowl LVIII in 2024.That detail matters because it places the network’s concerns well before the July 2026 arrest.Did Tony Romo’s arrest give CBS a way out?Romo was arrested on July 23 in Wisconsin for operating a vehicle while intoxicated. He later pleaded no contest to the OWI charge and received a six-month driving suspension and a fine. CBS placed him on leave, with J.J. Watt moving into the lead booth alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson.The arrangement has now become permanent. CBS confirmed that Watt will continue as the network’s lead NFL analyst for the remainder of the season.Marchand put the situation bluntly: “The arrest was not the reason; it was the excuse.” He also reported that the settlement covering the final four seasons and $72 million of Romo’s contract came because CBS wanted to move on.The exact financial terms of that settlement have not been disclosed. What is clear is that CBS chose to end a contract that still carried a major financial commitment. Romo’s departure therefore appears to have been about more than one night in Milwaukee. articles.title: Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. Trade Graded by NFL Insiders, 'They Were Bidding Against Themselves'
articles.summary: Some teams around the NFL feel the Dallas Cowboys paid too much to acquire cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday.
articles.body:
Some teams around the NFL feel the Dallas Cowboys paid too much to acquire cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday.

The Cowboys traded a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round for Porter, who had yet to play for the Steelers this season amid stalled contract negotiations and a back injury.

According to Jones, "many around the league believed Dallas overpaid, based largely on the belief that teams don't view Porter as a top-tier corner."

Jones also noted the Cowboys "have a strong recent history of overpaying for talent."

One executive told Jones about the Cowboys: "They were bidding against themselves for Porter."

Jones noted that some people around the NFL see the value of picks dropping the farther they are in the future. One general manager told Jones he would equate the value of the 2028 second-rounder to a third-round pick in 2027.

Porter was not listed with an injury designation on the Cowboys' latest injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Houston Texans.

The trade for Porter left the Cowboys with a projected four draft picks in 2027, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram.

The Steelers had at least one additional suitor for Porter. Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters after the trade his team was "very much in" on the cornerback.

Both the Lions, which have allowed the most passing yards against in the NFL, and the Cowboys, which are missing multiple key members of their secondary to injury, have reason to overpay for a boost to their defense.

Jones pointed out it's the Cowboys with a recent pattern of seemingly overpaying for players. That includes giving up draft capital for both Trey Lance and Joe Milton, neither of whom panned out as a reliable backup behind Dak Prescott

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said Friday in an appearance on 105.3 The Fan he saw the Porter trade as betting the player could reach new heights in Pittsburgh similar to the production boost enjoyed by George Pickens following his trade from the Steelers.

The Cowboys initially acquired Pickens last offseason in exchange for a 2026 third-round while swapping a 2027 fifth- and sixth-rounder.

That might have also seemed like an overpay had Pickens not gone on to record the best season of his career by racking up 93 catches for 1,429 receiving yards in 17 games.

Porter already allowed the third-lowest passer rating in the NFL last season, per PFF . He could establish himself as one of the league's top corners and set himself up for a big payday next offseason by following in Pickens' footsteps and putting together a resurgent campaign once he is able to make his season debut for Dallas.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Trade Value Analyzed by NFL Execs Amid Rumors on Cardinals WR's Future
articles.summary: Some people around the NFL reportedly remain unconvinced of Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr.'s future as a potential WR1, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones.
articles.body:
Some people around the NFL reportedly remain unconvinced of Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr.'s future as a potential WR1, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones .

Jones reported Friday that "multiple sources who have studied [Harrison's] 2026 tape do not see a receiver playing with the energy and effort of a No. 1 wideout."

Players Who Could Use a Change of Scenery 🏈

One AFC executive told Jones: "Forget where he was drafted, watch him play. He's like a third receiver with upside. He's not fast, not physical and doesn't do anything after the catch."

About whether the Cardinals will consider trading Harrison, another AFC executive told Jones, "When you get injured, stop seeing the ball, have drops and not in the most stable quarterback position to help get that page turned, it can weigh on young guys. Quite honestly it may be where he needs a change of scenery to be the best version of himself. But if you're Arizona, you want to keep as many assets as you can."

Harrison has recorded four catches for 73 yards during the Cardinals' 1-2 start to the 2026 season.

Most of the Cardinals' targets over that time have gone to tight end Trey McBride and wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Friday "the perception of Harrison from people around the league is that he isn't a fit in an Arizona offense that prioritizes McBride as its top target, and that has led some teams to think he might be available."

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , people around the NFL see Harrison's trade value as something around "a quality Day 3 pick."

Graziano noted, however, the Cardinals "have given no indication that they are eager or even interested in trading Harrison."

Harrison, the No. 4 pick of the 2024 draft, is signed through the 2027 season with a 2028 club option on his rookie contract .

Should the Cardinals decide to hold onto that deal and hope Harrison can continue developing, it wouldn't be their only recent investment into young offensive talent. The Cardinals used the No. 3 pick of the 2024 draft to add running back Jeremiyah Love.

Brissett is only signed through the 2026 season, so the Cardinals could hope to retool next season around a quarterback acquired either through free agency, the trade market or the 2027 draft.

In that case, the Cardinals could look to get Harrison more involved with their offense down the stretch. Brissett said after finding Harrison for a season-high three receptions in Week 3 he was "trying to find more ways to get him the ball."

The Cardinals also have McBride under contract to go alongside their recent extension for Wilson, limiting what targets might be available for Harrison. What kind of usage the third-year wideout sees going forward, starting Sunday with a Week 4 matchup at the New York Giants, could provide an indication of what the Cardinals are planning for his future.

articles.title: New Patriots Rumors on Drake Maye, Mike Vrabel Relationship Amid Report of Rift
articles.summary: NFL insider Tom Pelissero discredited rumors regarding a rift between New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and quarterback Drake Maye amid the team's 1-2 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
NFL insider Tom Pelissero discredited rumors regarding a rift between New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and quarterback Drake Maye amid the team's 1-2 start to the 2026 season.

Pelissero reported Saturday on his Substack "there were some chuckles among those in the know" about a report from WEEI's Greg Hill regarding an "issue" between Maye and Vrabel.

"Those who know both the coach and quarterback well say there's zero truth to the theory that there are problems with their relationship," Pelissero reported. "They speak regularly, never a tense word between them, and together were two of the driving forces behind last year's AFC title."

When asked about the rumors earlier this week, Vrabel said he came to New England specifically because he wanted to coach Maye as his quarterback.

"Believe it or not, I had choices to where I wanted to coach. I wanted to coach here, because Drake was the quarterback," Vrabel said Wednesday. "I don't have really much other to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source."

Vrabel was responding to Hill saying on his show he heard from an "insider" that "despite what Mike Vrabel may have said publicly, [the issue] goes back to Drake Maye not being his guy."

The report came after a rough season start that has seen Maye score one touchdown while throwing six interceptions.

That marks the most picks given up by a Patriots quarterback through three games since Drew Bledsoe in 1994.

That stretch was capped off by Maye throwing two interceptions in a 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, which marked Maye's 10th game with multiple turnovers since 2024.

Vrabel could be seen speaking with Maye on the sideline after his third turnover of the day late in the third quarter before benching his starter in favor of Tommy DeVito with eight minutes remaining in the blowout.

Maye has committed a combined 15 turnovers, including 10 interceptions and five fumbles, since the start of the 2025 playoffs.

Helping Maye regain confidence in his ball security will be key to Vrabel's hopes of turning the Patriots' season starting Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, which despite their perfect record have allowed the sixth-most passing yards against through three games.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Injury: Updates on Commanders QB's INJURY X and Return
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is expected to return/miss more time from a dislocated elbow.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is expected to return/miss more time from a dislocated elbow.

Per SOURCE X , Daniels is expected to be out X days/weeks .

Daniels dislocated his left elbow in the first half of Washington's 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. It's the same elbow he dislocated last season that kept him out for seven of the final eight games.

Ahead of the Commanders' Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts, Daniels returned to practice on a limited basis. He ultimately didn't play to give his injury more time to heal, but this was an encouraging sign his absence might not last much longer.

One reason the Commanders may have felt comfortable keeping Daniels out against the Colts is how well Marcus Mariota played in Week 3. He finished with 183 passing yards and three touchdowns in a 33-31 upset win over the Seattle Seahawks.

Given how prevalent the elbow issues have been for Daniels over the past two seasons, the Commanders want to be cautious to make sure he is at full strength before putting him back on the field.

Mariota's experience gives the Commanders a strong offensive floor when he is in games, but they need Daniels to reach whatever the ceiling for this team is going to be in 2026.

Daniels was 29-of-51 for 260 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions through the air in two games prior to the injury. He also ran for 100 yards on 12 carries during that period.

articles.title: Micah Parsons Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Packers Star's Timeline for Season Debut
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons' eligibility to come off the PUP list in Week 5 doesn't mean he'll be making an immediate return to his team, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons' eligibility to come off the PUP list in Week 5 doesn't mean he'll be making an immediate return to his team, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero .

Pelissero reported Saturday on his Substack Parsons "isn't expected to return to practice next week" because he "just isn't ready."

"While there have been no setbacks, it's possible that the five-time Pro Bowl selection won't play in a game until November," Pelissero reported.

Parsons suffered a torn ACL alongside meniscus damage in his left knee last December. He underwent reconstructive ACL surgery Dec. 29.

Parsons' PUP placement mandated his absence for the first four games of the season, a stretch that will wrap up Sunday with a Week 4 matchup at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur said earlier this week Parsons would not be joining his team for practice ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the visiting Chicago Bears.

"No setbacks. Just part of the process," LaFleur said Monday. "He's got to get cleared before we can let him get out there."

The upcoming game against the Bears is followed by a Week 6 reunion with Parsons' former teammates on the Dallas Cowboys. Parsons told reporters in August he saw that matchup as a "very realistic" return date.

Parsons added at the time he and his trainers would have to "put the work in" in order to continue rehabilitating from his surgery.

Waiting until November to return, which would give Parsons a full 11 months to recover from his ACL surgery, indicates Parsons could be back in the lineup at the earliest for a Week 9 game at the New England Patriots.

The Packers then play the visiting Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking a Week 11 bye.

Parsons recorded 12.5 sacks in 14 games of his first campaign with the Packers before going down with his season-ending injury.

The Packers could use the boost Parsons would add to their pass rush after a 1-2 start to the season, but waiting until Parsons is fully healthy will be key to making sure the star defensive end is available down the stretch of his four-year, $188 million contract.

articles.title: The Jets might be improved. But they still can’t intercept a pass.
articles.summary: Three weeks into the NFL season, after suffering two losses by a combined 10 points, New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn held his index finger and thumb inches apart to illustrate how close he felt his team was to a breakthrough.
articles.body: Three weeks into the NFL season, after suffering two losses by a combined 10 points, New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn held his index finger and thumb inches apart to illustrate how close he felt his team was to a breakthrough. “How do we close that gap?” Glenn said Sunday in Detroit, after a loss to the Lions that left the Jets 1-2. “I challenge myself, I challenge the staff, I even challenge the players on let’s identify a couple things that we need to improve on and let’s make sure that we hone in on those things.” One area isn’t hard to find: No team has been worse at intercepting passes in NFL history than the Jets. The league’s record-setting interceptionless streak grew to 20 games during New York’s Week 3 loss at Detroit. New York last picked off a pass on Jan. 5, 2025, when it recorded two. Ever since, the Jets’ defense has faced 608 passes with nary a pick to show for it. “That’s hard to do,” former NFL coach Jon Gruden said on social media this week. “You would think a ball would ricochet into somebody’s hands.” During Glenn’s 15-year playing career as a defensive back, interceptions were a specialty. He collected 41, tied for 73rd on the NFL’s all-time list. As the Jets’ streak grew last December, Glenn admitted that “it’s disappointing that we don’t have an interception because coming from what I’ve always played, you expect those things to happen.” The Jets know all about turnover. When Glenn was hired in January 2025, after a successful run as Detroit’s defensive coordinator, he was the franchise’s fifth coach since its last winning season in 2015. Glenn told fans to “expect a winning team that you will be proud of.” But only weeks into his first season, as the Jets staggered to a 3-14 record, the team traded two of its best defensive players in cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams. That defensive fire sale didn’t help a unit that would allow 29.6 points per game, the second most in the league. When the streak reached 12 games last December, Glenn called it “really puzzling.” When the streak reached 15 to break the previous record held by the San Francisco 49ers in 2024, Glenn said after a loss to New Orleans: “I hate the fact that we didn’t get an interception.” “But the thing is we got a turnover, and then we got a fourth-down stop, so these are some things we can build on.” Unfortunately for Glenn and the Jets, turnovers of any variety have been hard to come by. Since the start of the 2025 season, New York has forced a league-low six turnovers in 20 games. The next-lowest team produced 13. The league leader in that span, Chicago, has 39. New York set out to address its defensive shortcomings in the offseason. In its secondary, it signed safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, drafted a safety and cornerback and signed Nahshon Wright, whose five interceptions last season helped Chicago pick off a league best 23. Yes, Wright had heard of the streak. “I’m on social media, so I’ve seen it, but try not to pay it any mind,” Wright said in June. But “honestly, don’t think it’s been brought up at all” during team meetings, he added. “I think 2025 was 2025, and I think we’re trying to turn over a new leaf,” Wright said. Three games in, the Jets’ rank in the league’s upper half by allowing just 20.3 points per game. Yet the streak lives on. Relief could be on the way. In three weeks, New York faces New England, whose quarterback Drake Maye has thrown 10 interceptions in his last seven games. “We’re right here and our guys know it,” Glenn said, his fingers inches apart. “It’s this gap right here that we got to close. And we’re fighting our asses off to close that gap, and we will.”

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Top Trade Candidates Including Kayvon Thibodeaux, Brian Thomas Jr., More
articles.summary: Multiple players reportedly bear watching with regard to a potential trade leading up to the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10.
articles.body:
Multiple players reportedly bear watching with regard to a potential trade leading up to the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported Saturday that he spoke to sources who indicated that Pittsburgh Steelers linebackers Alex Highsmith, Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne, Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle Grover Stewart, New York Giants linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux, Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy and Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. are worth keeping an eye on when it comes to a possible trade.

However, Jones noted that all is "quiet" for now on the NFL trade front.

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

There has already been one major trade since the start of the regular season, as the Steelers sent cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys this week for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 sixth-round pick.

One of the biggest names mentioned by Jones that could be on the move is Thibodeaux, who was the No. 5 overall pick in the 2022 NFL draft.

Since setting a career high with 11.5 sacks in 2023, Thibodeaux has totaled just eight sacks. Part of that is due to the signing of Brian Burns and selection of Abdul Carter with the third overall pick in last year's draft.

Burns is set to miss the rest of the 2026 season with a torn ACL, but he is signed through 2028, as is Carter.

Thibodeaux is set to become a free agent at the conclusion of this season, though, and if the Giants have no plans to re-sign him, then trading him and recouping value makes a lot of sense.

Another name of interest is Thomas, who is not far removed from a spectacular rookie season in 2024.

After going 23rd overall to the Jags in the 2024 NFL draft, Thomas erupted for 87 receptions for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie, en route to being named a Pro Bowler.

His production experienced a sharp decline last season, though, as he finished with just 48 catches for 707 yards and two scores.

Through three games this season, Thomas has just seven grabs for 88 yards and no touchdowns, and he is clearly behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' wide receiver pecking order.

Jacksonville will have to make a decision on the team option in Thomas' contract for 2028 by next offseason, and if the Jags are leaning toward declining it, then trading him now could be a sensible move.

articles.title: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest NFL Rumors on Rams Star's Return Timeline After Surgery
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams reportedly have a positive outlook when it comes to the anticipated return of superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams reportedly have a positive outlook when it comes to the anticipated return of superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, the Rams are hopeful Garrett will be able to return from his knee injury against the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18 when he is first eligible to be activated off injured reserve.

Jones added that a source told him rumors and speculation of Garrett potentially missing six weeks would represent a "worst-case scenario," and a team source expressed their belief that Garrett will return on Oct. 25 against the Las Vegas Raiders.

After being limited during training camp, Garrett suited up for the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

The seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year did not look like himself, though, as he failed to record a counting stat on 40 defensive snaps played.

Coming out of that game, Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery on his knee and was placed on injured reserve, meaning he would have to miss the Rams' next two games.

Los Angeles has gone 1-1 without him, and the team is just 1-2 overall, which is somewhat surprising given the Rams' status as the unquestioned Super Bowl favorite entering the season.

Garrett's arrival is a big reason why the Rams were widely considered the team to beat in 2026.

He is coming off a historic campaign, as Garrett set the single-season NFL record with 23 sacks in 2025.

The Rams got aggressive and acquired him in a trade with the Cleveland Browns, sending pass-rusher Jared Verse and three draft picks in the other direction.

While the deal has not paid dividends for the Rams yet, there is still plenty of time for Garrett to make an impact, particularly if he returns shortly after he is eligible to come off IR.

articles.title: Odell Beckham's Jr.'s Impact on Malik Nabers Before Giants Release Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. may have had an impact on the New York Giants' 2026 season despite recording no catches in three games prior to his release.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. may have had an impact on the New York Giants' 2026 season despite recording no catches in three games prior to his release .

Beckham started off his return to the Giants by helping Malik Nabers complete his comeback from a major knee injury, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday.

"Beckham has been there for Nabers every step of the way, a team source tells me," Jones reported.

Jones added Beckham "has been huge for Nabers' confidence as he returned to action, drawing from Beckham's own experiences after he tore his ACL twice in his career."

Nabers suffered a torn ACL and damaged meniscus in Week 4 of last season. He initially underwent surgery in late October before undergoing a cleanup procedure during the offseason, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan .

He returned for Week 1 of the 2026 season, although his production has been limited in the wake of the season-ending injury Jaxson Dart suffered in Week 2.

Nabers said ahead of the Giants' Week 4 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals he was still working on establishing trust in his surgically-repaired knee.

"I want to do certain moves, but my mind is like, 'Ah, not yet'... [Darnell] Mooney talks to me about that. My teammates have been implementing confidence in me to just let go, just be free," Nabers said Thursday.

Beckham said ahead of the Giants' season opener he had spoken with Nabers about how there would be natural "fear and anxiety" involved in returning from a major knee injury, of which Beckham suffered two earlier in his NFL career.

"My advice for him is like, when you are ready and you feel it, that's when you come back," Beckham said ahead of Week 1 (h/t The Athletic's Dan Duggan ). "But at the same point in time, you're not going to feel like your one thousand percent self until some point in the early, middle of the season. It's just something that takes time."

Nabers may no longer be teammates with Beckham, who he previously described as the reason he started watching football, but he could still look to carry that lesson into what could be a bounce-back performance against a struggling Cardinals passing defense this Sunday in East Rutherford.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Puka Nacua's Rams Snap Count Ahead of Return From Injury
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua reportedly may not play a full allotment of snaps when he returns to the lineup Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua reportedly may not play a full allotment of snaps when he returns to the lineup Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, it was determined that Nacua did not need surgery on the groin injury that kept him out of L.A.'s past two games, but he "may be on a stricter snap count than usual" this week.

Still, Pelissero noted that there is "optimism" Nacua will be able to "make an impact" on the field this weekend.

In Week 1, Nacua led the Rams with five receptions for 74 yards, but they fell 27-7 to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Coming out of that game, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua had "a little bit of soreness" in his groin, and he went on to miss the team's win over the New York Giants in Week 2 and loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 3.

Nacua had been nursing a psoas injury during training camp, but McVay noted that the groin ailment was a separate issue.

In Nacua's absence, Davante Adams was clearly quarterback Matthew Stafford's top target in the passing game, as he went off for eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns against the Giants, and seven grabs for 137 yards against the Broncos.

While Adams is still a dangerous player and a potential future Hall of Famer, there is no question that Nacua is the Rams' WR1 when he is healthy and playing.

The 2023 fifth-round pick out of BYU is coming off a career season in 2025 that saw him lead the NFL with 129 receptions, while also recording 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns.

Nacua was named a Pro Bowler for the second time and a First Team All-Pro for the first time as a result.

Even if he is at less than 100 percent and doesn't play his usual amount of snaps, having Nacua back in Week 4 should be huge for the Los Angeles offense.

Nacua is going to command defensive attention whenever he is on the field, so even if passes aren't going his way, he figures to open things up for Adams and the Rams' other wide receivers and tight ends.

Sunday's road game against the Eagles is a big one for the Rams since a loss would drop them to 1-3 on the season, which is something few would have expected out of the preseason favorite to win the Super Bowl.

articles.title: “I’ve screwed up a lot”: Tom Brady's emotional confession about fatherhood, his three kids and the parenting lessons he’s still learning away from the NFL spotlight
articles.summary: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, but he does not pretend he has fatherhood figured out. On Nov.
articles.body: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, but he does not pretend he has fatherhood figured out. On Nov. 12, 2024, the former NFL quarterback spoke about parenting at the Fortune Global Forum in New York City. Brady admitted he has made mistakes while raising his three children, Jack, Benjamin and Vivian. His focus now is simple: stay dependable, support his kids and keep learning as they grow.Tom Brady admits fatherhood has come with plenty of mistakesDuring his Fortune Global Forum appearance on Nov. 12, 2024, Brady called parenting one of the hardest jobs people take on. He also pushed back on the idea that his NFL success makes him an expert father.“Being a parent is probably the hardest job all of us have and we screwed up a lot and I’ve screwed up a lot as a parent,” Brady said at the event.He then explained what he tries to give his three children instead of a perfect parenting formula. Brady said he wants to be “dependable and consistent” for them.Brady also spoke about the pressure his children face because of their family name. During his June 2, 2023 interview with TODAY.com, he said his children did not choose the expectations that come with having famous parents. He wants them to find something they enjoy and build friendships with people who value them for who they are, not because of their parents.That approach fits with something he said earlier about raising his children. TB-12 told Entertainment Tonight that he and Gisele Bündchen wanted to give Benjamin and Vivian a strong foundation as they grew up. He said they were still learning alongside their children. Tom Brady wants his children to build their own pathsBrady also understands the pressure that comes with his surname. His children have grown up with a father whose NFL career includes seven Super Bowl wins, so expectations can follow them before they make their own choices.Jack, Brady’s eldest son with Bridget Moynahan, has also taken a different sporting path from his father. At the Nov. 12, 2024 Fortune event, Brady spoke about Jack’s interest in basketball. He joked about his son’s jumping ability but made his support clear.“I want him to know that his dad’s got his back,” Brady said at the forum.Brady has also spoken about the pressure his children face because of their parents. In a June 2, 2023 interview with TODAY.com, he said his children face expectations because of who their mother and father are, even though they never chose that spotlight.His message has stayed consistent: his children need room to become themselves.For Brady, that also means accepting that parenting will keep changing. articles.title: Baker Mayfield Injury Update, Latest NFL Rumors on Bucs QB's Recovery, Return Timeline
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has taken a step in his recovery from a dislocated right thumb that could potentially allow him to return a bit sooner than expected, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has taken a step in his recovery from a dislocated right thumb that could potentially allow him to return a bit sooner than expected, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday.

Mayfield, who suffered the injury to his throwing hand in a Week 3 game against the Minnesota Vikings, has already been ruled out for Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Pelissero reported on his Substack that Mayfield is "scheduled to get stitches removed from his right thumb on Monday—an important step as Mayfield pushes to return to action as soon as possible."

Bucs coach Todd Bowles told reporters Monday Mayfield would be sidelined for at least three weeks with the injury. Mayfield "hopes to beat that timeline," Pelissero reported.

"He got good news from tests that showed no fracture or ligament or tendon damage," Pelissero reported. "Now it's a matter of reducing the swelling and removing the stitches, which bother him when he grips the football. There's also a healing process that must take place after the stitches are out, and he has to be able to grip the ball without stability issues."

Pelissero estimated it would be "tough, but not impossible" for Mayfield to return for Week 5.

Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will be under center against the Packers. The Bucs are then scheduled to play at the Dallas Cowboys on short rest Thursday night before hosting the Pittsburgh Steelers 10 days later.

Bowles said he didn't expect Mayfield to need surgery or a trip to the injured reserve, indicating he expected the quarterback by at least a Week 7 matchup at the Carolina Panthers.

Mayfield suffered the injury when his thumb bent back on a hit by Vikings defender Blake Cashman after throwing an interception in the fourth quarter of the Bucs' Week 3 loss last Sunday.

He underwent an MRI the following day which revealed no fracture, no ligament damage and no tendon damage, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Mayfield was spotted at practice this week with his injured thumb immobilized, per Pewter Report.

Mayfield completed 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 passing yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions prior to his injury on the Bucs' way to an 0-3 start.

Only seven teams have recovered from an 0-3 record to make the playoffs, per NBC Sports' Mike Florio .

The 1992 Chargers are the only team to qualify for the postseason after starting a season with four straight losses.

Daniels will be tasked with keeping the Bucs afloat until Mayfield is able to return by leading the team to victory in his first NFL start Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Tampa.

articles.title: Sean Payton comments on NFL-best record in October: ‘I didn’t know that’
articles.summary: Sean Payton is an mid-season maestro
articles.body:
When it comes to September, the Denver Broncos have not been a very good team. When the calendar turns to October, the Broncos and specifically coach Sean Payton have turned up the heat, and played some of their best football of the year.

Payton has an all-time 54-17 in October , good for the best month mark in NFL history, including a perfect month in 2025 with wins over the Philadelphia Eagles , Dallas Cowboys, New York Giants and New York Jets, which turned Denver from 2-2 to 6-2 during that stretch.

"I have no idea (about that stat), Payton said leading into Week 4. "I didn't know that, but I think that the coach in you says, 'Man, why isn't it better in September?' So hopefully we can continue that. Just leaving the team as we called everyone up, it was, 'October was good for us a year ago, and that's because you guys made it a priority during the week.'"

The Broncos in 2026 have a similarly difficult October ahead of them, with the Los Angeles Chargers, San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals on deck. After finishing September 2-1, Payton is ready for the challenge ahead.

"We're early in this race," Payton said. "We have to be finding these areas that don't become another mistake Week 5 or Week 6. So I don't recall— you don't remember Octobers specifically, but hopefully we can continue that trend."\

The Broncos look to start October off strong against the 49ers, who they play on Sunday at 2:25 pm MST.

articles.title: “Don’t Give Two F’s”: Liam Coen Shuts Down Travis Hunter Noise Over 2-Way Star’s Usage By Jags
articles.summary: Due to Travis Hunter getting minimal snaps on offense, the Jacksonville Jaguars star’s performance is hard to measure, given his high draft pick. Although he...
articles.body:
Due to Travis Hunter getting minimal snaps on offense, the Jacksonville Jaguars star's performance is hard to measure, given his high draft pick. Although he has helped drive head coach Liam Coen's squad to the league's top-scoring defense.

Liam Coen Defends Two-Way Star Travis Hunter's Role

Head coach Liam Coen brushed off the noise surrounding his star player's playing time. He explained that the Jaguars' top priority is team success rather than managing individual metrics: "He cares about winning," Coen said in the press conference. "That's what he cares about. Like, and all the other stuff, the reps, where we picked him, does that — I don't give two Fs about value. And neither does he. We care about winning. And that's it."

Earlier in May, Hunter, on external noise to dual-position play, said , "That room goes both ways. I go in there every single day for about 15, 30 minutes throughout the day. Just going there and continuously burn out reps. I can burn out 30, 40 reps in 15 minutes every time I go in there."

Last season, Hunter made it clear he would rather walk away from the entire sport than accept a single-position restriction:

"It's never playing football again," he said . "Because I've been doing it my whole life, and I love being on the football field. I feel like I could dominate on each side of the ball, so I really enjoy doing it."

A major knee injury cut short Hunter's debut season. The Jaguars (who picked him second overall in 2024 NFL Draft) are easing him back into the offense.

articles.title: Dave Portnoy’s Ryan Day accusation raises questions after Barstool Sports is removed from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff

Portnoy claims Day and Ohio State pressured the Big Ten and Fox after their long-running tension. However, reporting from The Athletic says there was no single incident behind the decision. Huge dollars at stake, and you have Cryin Ryan throwing temper tantrums and making threats every few days on something I said,” Portnoy added.Portnoy then took another direct shot at the Ohio State coach.“I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy s**t even I didn’t realize he was this soft #Goblue,” he wrote.Those are Portnoy’s claims, not an established account of what happened. articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is reportedly set to take an important step in his recovery from a dislocated right thumb as he attempts to r...
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is reportedly set to take an important step in his recovery from a dislocated right thumb as he attempts to return ahead of his initial three-week timeline.

NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that Mayfield is scheduled to have the stitches removed from his injured thumb Monday.

"Bucs QB Baker Mayfield is scheduled to have stitches removed from his thumb Monday — an important step as he pushes to beat the three-week timeline for returning," Pelissero wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Mayfield suffered the injury late in Tampa Bay's 23-16 Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings last Sunday. The quarterback injured his throwing hand on a fourth-quarter play when he was hit while attempting a pass that was intercepted. He left the game and did not return for the Buccaneers' final possession.

An MRI later revealed no fracture or tendon damage, and head coach Todd Bowles announced that Mayfield was expected to miss a minimum of three weeks. The injury also ended Mayfield's streak of 57 consecutive starts since joining Tampa Bay in 2023.

Buccaneers turn to Jalon Daniels as Baker Mayfield continues recovery

Before suffering the injury, Mayfield completed 17 of 34 passes for 217 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Minnesota. Through three games this season, the veteran has completed 61 of 96 passes for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while posting an 80.0 passer rating. Tampa Bay lost all three of those starts.

The Buccaneers will now turn to rookie Jalon Daniels as they attempt to earn their first victory of the 2026 season. Daniels is set to make his first NFL start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers after replacing Mayfield late in the loss to Minnesota.

Tampa Bay enters the Week 4 matchup at 0-3, while Green Bay sits at 1-2. The Buccaneers and Packers will kick off Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX.

Mayfield will not be available for that matchup, but having his stitches removed Monday represents another step toward returning to the field. If he can beat the original three-week recovery timeline, the Buccaneers could get their starting quarterback back sooner than initially expected as they attempt to recover from their winless start.
